title: Do-It-Yourself Tranquilizers That Bring Peace of Mind
coreMove: The do-it-yourself tranquilizer is learned nonresponse: notice the signal, relax the body, delay old reflexes, and answer only what serves the goal.

exampleSpecs.audience: Donna, a reader learning to separate signals from obedience
exampleSpecs.stakes: A harmless interruption can either run the body or become a training rep.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show the ringing telephone in the den as a conditioned response Donna can refuse.

exampleSpecs.audience: Nicholas, a team lead delaying anger before it becomes conduct
exampleSpecs.stakes: One sharp sentence could turn a fixable report error into a defensive room.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use count backward from 10 to interrupt anger and create delay.

exampleSpecs.audience: Arlo, a clinic supervisor holding steady under emotional weather
exampleSpecs.stakes: A tense waiting room can spread its climate into the staff unless he sets a steadier point.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use 98.6 degrees, body temperature, thermostat, and emotional climate as the stabilizing analogy.

exampleSpecs.audience: Zainab, a board chair filtering interruption by goal relevance
exampleSpecs.stakes: A public interruption could become the whole meeting if she obeys the provocation.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Transfer the telephone-in-the-den lesson to an off-course public signal.

exampleSpecs.audience: Hudson, a consultant revising an angry response before sending
exampleSpecs.stakes: A defensive email could make a repairable client concern permanent.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show count backward from 10 creating delay before anger locks into action.

exampleSpecs.audience: Kwame, a coach setting emotional climate after a bad call
exampleSpecs.stakes: A young team will copy either his steady set point or his flare of irritation.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Apply the 98.6-degree body thermostat image to emotional steadiness in motion.
